article_title: Advancing understanding of learning experience design: refining and clarifying definitions using an eDelphi study approach
citation: Tawfik, A., Schmidt, M., Payne, L., & Huang, R. (2024). Advancing understanding of learning experience design: refining and clarifying definitions using an eDelphi study approach. Education Tech Research Dev. https://doi.org/10.1007/s11423-024-10355-z
title: Learning experience design (LXD) as a human-centered, transdisciplinary approach to designing learning experiences
description: The article defines LXD as a perspective on learning design that goes beyond content development to consider the broader human experience of interacting with learning environments. Building on Schmidt and Huang (2022), LXD is characterized as "a human-centric, theoretically-grounded, and socio-culturally sensitive approach to learning design, intended to propel learners towards identified learning goals, and informed by UXD methods". The eDelphi findings refine this definition, situating LXD alongside instructional design rather than as a separate field, and emphasizing transdisciplinarity across HCI, UXD, and learning design.
requirements: Consensus among practitioners about the elements that comprise LXD, established through systematic and collaborative approaches such as eDelphi studies
constraints: Experts did not agree that LXD is a discrete field of study or a unique phenomenon with its own characteristics, methods, and processes; LXD is positioned as an emergent perspective within the existing field of instructional design
target_learners: All learners in technology-mediated learning environments
target_learning_goals: Knowledge construction through human-centered design of learning experiences
key_sources: Tawfik, A., Schmidt, M., Payne, L., & Huang, R. (2024). Advancing understanding of learning experience design: refining and clarifying definitions using an eDelphi study approach. Education Tech Research Dev. https://doi.org/10.1007/s11423-024-10355-z

article_title: Supporting children’s engagement through learning experience design, situational interest, and user experience: implementing a blended learning math experience in the classroom
citation: Joseph T. Wong, Jessica Cai, Isabelle S. Lerner, Jiwon Lee, Lindsey Engle Richland. (2026). Supporting children's engagement through learning experience design, situational interest, and user experience: implementing a blended learning math experience in the classroom. Education Tech Research Dev. https://doi.org/10.1007/s11423-026-10637-8
title: Learning experience design (LXD) as a learner-centered, goal-oriented, interdisciplinary course design framework
description: The article presents LXD as a design framework extending beyond traditional instructional design, defined as "creating learning situations that extend beyond the formal classroom learning environment and often integrate online and virtual technological formats". It adopts Floor's (2018) five fundamentals: human-centered, goal-oriented, grounded in theories of learning, learning through practice, and heavily interdisciplinary. In this study the authors implemented the LXD framework to build a blended learning pedagogical approach integrating interactive video-based mathematics for elementary students in the classroom.
requirements: The article states LXD employs one or more pedagogical frameworks that serve as the basis for the learning theories operationalized in the course
constraints: The article notes further research and practical applications of LXD are needed to enhance educational practices and meet the diverse needs of learners in various learning environments
examples: The authors applied the LXD framework to guide iterative design revisions of a blended proportional reasoning course, building on a beta online course from the COVID-19 pandemic
key_sources: Joseph T. Wong, Jessica Cai, Isabelle S. Lerner, Jiwon Lee, Lindsey Engle Richland. (2026). Supporting children's engagement through learning experience design, situational interest, and user experience: implementing a blended learning math experience in the classroom. Education Tech Research Dev. https://doi.org/10.1007/s11423-026-10637-8

article_title: Learning experience design with immersive virtual reality in physics education
citation: Yiannis Georgiou, Olia Tsivitanidou, Andri Ioannou. (2023). Learning experience design with immersive virtual reality in physics education. https://zenodo.org
title: LX design pattern combining an immersive VR simulation with inquiry-based learning for complex scientific phenomena
description: The article presents a learning experience (LX) design that integrates an immersive VR simulation into an inquiry-based learning environment in Physics classrooms. The design is motivated by the argument that immersive VR simulations support learning of "complex scientific phenomena" via realistic graphics and interactions students can hardly experience otherwise. The pattern was enacted and evaluated with high-school students learning the Special Theory of Relativity.
requirements: An immersive VR simulation of the target scientific phenomenon
An inquiry-based learning process within which the simulation is embedded
constraints: The record states that integration of immersive VR in science classrooms introduces new challenges and that learning designs to inform practice are lacking
target_learning_goals: Conceptual understanding of complex scientific phenomena, here the Special Theory of Relativity
examples: The LX design was enacted with 109 high-school students in Physics classrooms covering the Special Theory of Relativity
key_sources: Yiannis Georgiou, Olia Tsivitanidou, Andri Ioannou. (2023). Learning experience design with immersive virtual reality in physics education. https://zenodo.org

article_title: Learning experience design with immersive virtual reality in physics education
citation: Yiannis Georgiou, Olia Tsivitanidou, Andri Ioannou. (2023). Learning experience design with immersive virtual reality in physics education. https://zenodo.org
title: Learning experience (LX) design framework for integrating immersive VR in inquiry-based science learning
description: The article offers a learning experience (LX) design as an organizing framework for bringing an immersive VR simulation into an inquiry-based learning environment in Physics. The design specifies how the simulation and the inquiry process together support students' understanding of the Special Theory of Relativity. The authors "reflect on our LX design" after enactment and highlight questions for further research, positioning the design as a contribution to practice where learning designs are lacking.
requirements: An immersive VR simulation of the scientific phenomenon
An inquiry-based learning process in which the simulation is enacted
constraints: The record notes integration challenges and a lack of learning designs to inform practice; detailed design specifications are in restricted files
target_learners: High-school students (10-11th graders) in Physics classrooms
target_learning_goals: Conceptual understanding of the Special Theory of Relativity
examples: The LX design was enacted and evaluated with 109 high-school students using a mixed-method approach
key_sources: Yiannis Georgiou, Olia Tsivitanidou, Andri Ioannou. (2023). Learning experience design with immersive virtual reality in physics education. https://zenodo.org
